evidence.requirements: Everything in the brief is met. The start page shows title, date and time, "EUR n per guest" and "<n> seats left" (StartPage.tsx:24-33, start.jpg). Each tasting has a "Book <title>" link (StartPage.tsx:34-36). The form has "Name", "Email" and "Guests" fields (1–8) and a "Book" button (BookingPage.tsx:97-145). Errors appear next to the field they concern (form.jpg). The server rejects bookings that exceed the seats left with a message on the guests field (app.ts:82-85). The confirmation has the heading "Booking confirmed", the tasting, guests, total and reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx:33-46, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a "Password" field and a "Sign in" button checked against STAFF_PASSWORD (StaffPage.tsx:41-61, app.ts:54). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a "Cancel" button that frees seats (StaffPage.tsx:113-151, staff.jpg, store.ts:60). There is a fully booked state (BookingPage.tsx:45-48, tastings.ts:65). The stack is React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. Bookings are in memory and PORT defaults to 3000 (index.ts:8). Phone layout relies on responsive grid classes (sm:/lg:grid-cols, md:grid-cols) and overflow-x on the staff table; there is no mobile screenshot to confirm it.
evidence.correctness: Checking seats and inserting the booking happen in one synchronous call, so concurrent requests cannot oversell (store.ts:43-50). Seats left are recomputed from the live bookings, so cancelling frees seats automatically (store.ts:23-29). The schema trims the name, limits it to 100 characters, validates the email, and requires guests to be a whole number from 1 to 8; NaN and strings get a clear message (booking.ts). Server field errors are mapped onto the form fields (BookingPage.tsx:77-80), and the 409 response gives singular/plural and "fully booked" wording (app.ts:47-50). References avoid look-alike characters and are checked for collisions (store.ts:31-38). The booking page guards against stale results when the route changes (BookingPage.tsx:10,23). Minor gaps: malformed JSON falls through to Express's default HTML 400, which the client shows as a generic error, and a failed sign-out call (StaffPage.tsx:91-94) is an unhandled rejection.
evidence.security: The password check hashes both values with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual, and fails when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (staff.ts:16-20). Session tokens are 32 random bytes held server-side with an 8-hour expiry (staff.ts:41-43,53-62). The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, and Secure when the request is HTTPS (app.ts:10,100-104). Failed sign-ins lock out an IP after 5 attempts in 15 minutes (staff.ts:46-49). Sign-out invalidates the token on the server (staff.ts:64-66). Staff endpoints are protected by middleware (app.ts:60-63). React escapes all output, there are no secrets in the code, and the public booking lookup leaves out name and email (app.ts:30-37, test at bookings-api.test.ts:115-127). There is no helmet or other security-header middleware, which is a minor gap.
evidence.code_quality: Server, shared and client code are cleanly separated (server/, shared/, src/). The store and auth are small factory functions with dependencies injected (env, now) so they can be tested (app.ts:52). The zod schema is shared by client and server (shared/booking.ts). Names are clear and result types are discriminated unions (store.ts:14, staff.ts:9). TypeScript runs in strict mode, with ESLint configured. Each page component is small and handles loading, error and not-found states. The code is sized to the problem, with no needless layers.
evidence.tests: Four Vitest/supertest files exercise the API end to end. They cover the catalogue values, booking success, total and seat reduction, rejection above the seats left with the exact messages, fully booked, per-field validation errors, the 404s, grouping in staff bookings, cancelling freeing seats, 401s without a session, cookie attributes, the 8-hour expiry, lockout and its reset window, and sign-out invalidation. Schema boundaries (0, 9, 2.5, NaN, 100 and 101 characters) are tested (booking-schema.test.ts). There are no frontend or component tests, so the field labels, button texts, errors appearing next to fields, the fully booked form state and the staff UI flow are untested. Concurrent booking is not tested.
evidence.ux_design: Burgundy, cream and gold colours with serif headings give a coherent, polished winery look (start.jpg, staff.jpg). The cards are clear and the form shows a live total (form.jpg). The success notice is green and the reference is prominent (confirmation.jpg). The error state uses a red border and red text (form.jpg). Staff tables are clean, and empty groups say "No bookings" (staff.jpg). Weaknesses: the design is plain (no imagery, no footer or contact details), and the header is just a wordmark. Fully booked tastings still show an active-looking "Book" button on the start page (StartPage.tsx:34). "Cancel" acts at once with no confirmation and no success message (StaffPage.tsx:80-89). Loading states are bare text.
evidence.accessibility: Every input has a label tied to it with htmlFor/id. Invalid fields get aria-invalid, and aria-describedby points to the error, which has role="alert" (BookingPage.tsx:97-135, StaffPage.tsx:43-57). The page sets lang="en" (index.html:2). There are focus-visible outlines on inputs and buttons (index.css:50,62-70). The tables use th headers, with an sr-only label for the actions column (StaffPage.tsx:129). Details use dl/dt/dd, and the heading hierarchy is sensible. The muted grey #6f6461 on cream passes AA. Minor gaps: errors set from server responses via setError do not move focus, several role="alert" elements can fire at once, and the header has no nav landmark or skip link.
evidence.simplicity: There are 9 runtime dependencies, all mainstream and each with a purpose (express, cookie-parser, react, react-router, react-hook-form, zod, resolvers, tsx). The source is about 700 lines, with no database or extra state library. Running tsx in production avoids a separate server build. The amount of code fits the problem.
evidence.maintainability: The README gives the commands, environment variables and a note that data is kept in memory (README.md). There are OpenSpec specs for the three capabilities and a GLOSSARY. package-lock.json is present, and there are typecheck and lint scripts. The tests run in isolation from one another. Missing: there is no CI pipeline. engines is ">=22", not pinned, and there is no .nvmrc. There are no ADRs or decision records beyond the code comments marked "shortcut" (store.ts:19, staff.ts:11). There is no staff manual explaining how to sign in and cancel. There is no changelog or release approach beyond version 1.0.0. The trust-proxy option needed behind a reverse proxy is not documented in the README.

strengths: Correct booking logic: checking seats and inserting the booking happen in one synchronous call, seats left are derived from live bookings so cancelling frees seats, and one zod schema validates on both client and server with clear errors per field

Strong staff security: SHA-256 hashing with timingSafeEqual, random server-side session tokens with expiry, HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict/Secure cookies, lockout after failed sign-ins, and sign-out that invalidates the session on the server
Meaningful API tests covering seat limits, boundary values, cancelling, session expiry and lockout, plus a clean, small, well-structured codebase with OpenSpec specs
issues: Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, Node version not pinned (engines >=22, no .nvmrc), no ADRs, staff manual or changelog, and the trust-proxy deployment setting is missing from the README
No frontend tests: the field labels, button texts, errors appearing next to fields, the fully booked form state and the staff UI are untested

Rough UX edges: "Cancel" acts immediately with no confirmation or success message, fully booked tastings keep an active-looking "Book" button, and the design is plain (no imagery, footer or winery contact details)
review.verdict: This is a correct, secure and well-structured app that meets every requirement in the brief, with a coherent winery look and solid API tests. It is nearly ready to ship. It lacks a CI pipeline, frontend tests, a staff manual and a pinned Node version, and the staff cancel flow needs a confirmation step.
